argument: This finding supplies the missing magnitude for the open t-02 refute: the size of the migration, measured with greps the orchestrator can re-run from the sources directory. Read the counts as rewording sites (lines) and mentions (occurrences on those lines). Item one, the seven weapon properties, is BIGGER than the round-1 shape implied. 38 lines across four files need rewording, carrying 60 property mentions — not two definition lists of seven items each. Breakdown: 7 definition bullets in 15-equipment (`grep -A9 '^\*Properties:\*' 15-equipment | grep -c '^- \*'`); 7 headwords in 21-glossary (`grep -cE 'weapon propert' 21-glossary`), worded independently of the chapter list and therefore not a reprint that can be left alone; 10 of the 17 weapon rows in 15-equipment carry property cells, totalling 19 mentions (`grep -A20 'table.header(\[Weapon\]' 15-equipment | grep -oE '\b(Finesse|Versatile|Reach|Thrown|Light|Loading|Two-Handed)\b' | wc -l`); the 22-reference-sheets reprint carries the same 10 rows and 19 mentions; and three prose sites state a property as a rule about how damage resolves (15-equipment line 200, 08-disciplines lines 230 and 232). The propagation cost a per-definition budget cannot see is the 38 property mentions sitting inside the two table columns: rewording one property definition touches 20 weapon rows in two files. Item two, the weapon lists inside loadouts, is SMALLER than the round-1 reading. 18 lines and 24 weapon tokens in total: 9 class kit lines carrying 12 weapon tokens plus 2 shield and 6 armor-name tokens in 05-classes, and 9 equipment lines carrying 12 weapon tokens plus 2 shield tokens in 02-character-creation. The weapon subset is 24 tokens, not 43 listed entries; the remaining 31 entries are armor, tools, robes, focuses and packs and need no property rewording, so the t-01 argument built on per-item rewrite cost is roughly a third the size it looks. Item three, downstream consumers, is LARGER at the margins. In 20-bestiary, 15 attack lines are named for a catalog weapon and 2 Multiattack rules also name one, so the weapon-named rule count is 17 rather than 15, while 18 lines name a weapon or shield anywhere. In 17-magic-items, 6 item Type fields are typed on a catalog weapon or shield (Longsword twice, Warhammer, Dagger, Longbow, Shield) and a further 6 body lines name the dagger for Shadow Thorn. In 21-glossary, 10 named-item lines include the 6 property headwords that name their item lists, so those lines do double duty. In 22-reference-sheets, 22 weapon/shield lines plus 8 armor rows. Distinct lines across the three items: 119. Finally, the noise floor: grepping the property names raw returns 88 case-sensitive hits across the nine files, of which 28 are a different concept wearing the same word (7 Human-ancestry Versatile tokens in character creation, 6 armor-class Light tokens in the armor chapter, 5 armor-class Light tokens in the equipment chapter, 3 monster attack ranges plus 1 Light Sensitivity ability in the bestiary, 3 armor-class Light tokens and 1 trait mention in the glossary, 3 armor-class Light tokens in the reference sheet). True property mentions: 60. Any budget from a raw grep over-counts by about a third. Net verdict: larger than round 1 implied for the properties and the downstream references, smaller for the class kits.

evidence.claim: The chapter's property definitions are 7 bullets, and each bullet names the specific items that carry the property, so deleting the item names dangles the definition itself. 8 property mentions sit in these 7 lines.

- *Finesse*, use Agility instead of Brawn for attack and damage (Dagger, Shortsword, Throwing Dagger)
- *Reach*, can attack targets 10 ft away (Spear, Halberd)
- *Thrown*, can be thrown (range 20/60 ft: Dagger, Handaxe, Spear, Throwing Dagger)
- *Light*, can be used as an off-hand weapon for two-weapon fighting (Dagger, Shortsword, Handaxe)
- *Loading*, requires a Maneuver to reload between shots (Crossbow only)

evidence.claim: Noise floor. A raw case-sensitive grep for the seven property names over the nine sources returns 88 tokens, but 28 are a different concept using the same word, leaving 60 true property mentions. Worked computation: 02-character-creation +7 (all Human-ancestry trait, e.g. line 64); 16-armor-shields +6 (all armor weight class); 15-equipment +5 (armor weight class at lines 42, 79, 232, 233, 234); 20-bestiary +4 (3 monster attack ranges at 182, 503, 603 plus 1 Light Sensitivity ability at 597); 21-glossary +3 (trait at 97, armor weight class twice at 117); 22-reference-sheets +3 (armor weight class rows at 346, 347, 348). 7+6+5+4+3+3 = 28; 88-28 = 60.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: 88 tokens total; 28 non-property (trait/weight-class/attack-range homonyms); 60 true property mentions = 68.2% precision, i.e. a raw grep over-counts by 31.8%.

evidence.claim: Size verdict against the round-1 shape. The property item measures 38 lines where the round-1 framing of seven properties in two copies implies 14 lines, because the two table property columns add 38 mentions over 20 rows that a per-definition budget does not count. The loadout item measures 24 weapon tokens where the round-1 framing of 43 listed entries implies 43, because 31 entries are armor, tools, robes, focuses or packs. The downstream item measures 17 bestiary weapon-named rules, 6 magic-item Type fields plus 6 body lines, 10 glossary lines and 30 reference-sheet lines. Distinct lines across the three items: 38 + 18 + 69 = 125 line-entries, 119 after de-duplicating the 6 glossary lines counted in both the property item and the named-item item.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: properties 38 sites / 60 mentions; loadouts 18 lines / 24 weapon tokens; downstream 17+12+10+30 = 69 line-entries; 38+18+69 = 125 line-entries; distinct union 119 after removing the 6 glossary lines counted twice.
